thread:
cheng: heads-up — hit a weird correctness window in staging while doing a prefix ownership handoff + fastpath reads. low repro rate but deterministic when I force timing.

cheng: short timeline: 1) shard A decides to hand off prefix P to shard B, B starts populating residency and takes a soft lease. 2) a fastpath read arrives at B, sees cached prefix metadata but no committed residency token yet and returns a stale result. 3) concurrently, A still has in-flight write that should have been visible and ends up applied after B's read.

anika: can you paste the simplified repro and the state checks you used?

cheng: yeah — boiled down to this ordering, simplified pseudolog:

```
// A: owner -> A
A: write(k) -> apply
A: start handoff(prefix P -> B)
B: create soft-lease(epoch=42)
B: fastpath_read(k) // reads based on cached metadata
A: finish write(k) // should have been visible to reads on B
```

cheng: the issue is B's fastpath uses cached KV index + prefix bloom from before the write. when ownership moves, we don't have a clear fence that prevents those fastpath reads from being served until we've applied any inflight writes that A had.

maria: hmm. sounds like classic read-after-handoff reorder. Two obvious approaches: (1) introduce a takeover fence token that B must acquire and validate against A before fastpath reads are allowed, or (2) make the fastpath check consult an epoch vector / last-applied timestamp and reject fastpath if it's stale, falling back to a consistent read.

jamie: +1 on both options. tradeoffs: fence token gives a simple linearizable boundary but adds a hop during takeover (A -> control plane -> B or a sequencer). epoch check is cheaper but we need a global notion of "last applied" per-prefix; that's painful with concurrent multi-writer workloads.

anika: is there an option to make fastpath reads consult a cheap lease-validity bit that we flip atomically? e.g., when A initiates handoff it sets prefix.state = MIGRATING and writes a small handoff record. B refuses fastpath until it sees that record committed. that record is small — maybe one paxos/raft op — and could be piggybacked on handoff.

maria: that is basically a fencing record. the key question is correctness vs latency: if handoff rate is low this is fine. if we have frequent churn we pay a Paxos latency on many handoffs. we should quantify handoff QPS in Dedicated workload vs Hosted.

cheng: in staging I measured handoff durations ~20–50ms, and the added fence RTT would add ~10–20ms on takeover. acceptable for rare handoffs. problem is hotkey migrations (we auto-migrate hot prefixes) — those happen more often.

jamie: alternative: optimistic fastpath with a quick read-validate step. serve from cache but return a short validation token to caller; on next request we compare token against observed epoch. if mismatch, retry. That moves cost to rare retries but complicates client semantics.

anika: hmm clients already expect idempotent reads; retries are ok for internal RPCs but external API surface might expose flakiness. we can hide retries in service layer.

ops-bot: staging-metrics: prefix-migration-rate=12/min, fastpath-stale-detects=0.02% over last 24h, retry-latency-p99=120ms.

maria: given metrics, seems like a lightweight fencing record is simplest and safest. propose: on handoff, source writes a small handoff-record with monotonic epoch and pending_reads_allowed=false. target waits for that record, then installs residency and flips pending_reads_allowed=true. fastpath reads check pending_reads_allowed and epoch to decide.

cheng: that covers correctness. potential gotcha: what if source crashes after writing record but before draining in-flight writes? record must be written after source ensures no outstanding mutating ops for that prefix: i.e., serializable drain step. need clear owner drain protocol in RFC.

jamie: we should add an explicit "drain_ack" step: source quiesces mutations for prefix, writes handoff_record(epoch=n, drained=true), then hands off. target sees drained=true and knows no inflight mutates remain.

anika: action items: 1) cheng: sketch the owner drain + handoff record state machine (unit tests + invariants). 2) jamie: quick perf sim of fence RTT overhead under hotkey migration rates. 3) maria: update RFC appendix about migration cost and failure modes. I'll add invariant tests to our kv-cache integration suite.

cheng: sounds good — I'll post a tiny spike branch with a fake fence record and a deterministic unit that reproduces the bug. link will follow. thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: also flagging for eng-sre review for oncall behavior during partial handoff failures. and add an observability metric: handoff_record_latency and handoff_inconsistent_reads_count.

jamie: +1, will own canary rollout plan once spike is green.

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-4721 "prefix handoff fence + drain protocol" assigned to cheng, jira: https://redwood.company/INF-4721

cheng: FYI — repro branch: https://git.redwood/infr/runtime/kv-fence-spike (WIP).
